To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the entanglement temperature of excited states is given by the local temperature of the entanglement energy density, the change in the entaglement entropy of excited state with respect to a ground state is given by the change in the entropy of the reduced density matrix, and the change in the reduced density matrix of the excited state with respect the ground state is given in terms of the change in the local temperature.

the entanglement temperature of a ground state of a CFT is given by the inverse of its entanglement entropy density, that the first law-like relation between changes in the entangement entropy and conserved charges is valid for all excited states in any number of dimensions, and that the first law for excited states can be used to derive constraint equations on the entanglement of excited states.

we derived a general relation between ground state entangLEMENT Hamiltonian and physical stress tensor, reproduced the local ground state Hamiltonian, derived a local first law for entanglement entropy, derived the holographic equations for entanglement of excited states in CFT, and found a discrepancy with holographic results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the entanglement structure of excited states in quantum field theory and its holographic dual.
the entanglement properties of excited states in quantum field theory and holography.
the properties of entanglement in conformal field theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have provided a field theoretic derivation of the entanglement temperature and first law for excited states, and have shown that the entanglement of excited states in CFT is not well understood.
the entanglement temperature and the entanglement energy density are well defined in a quantum field theory, but that there are some discrepancies with the holographic results.
the entanglement temperature is a well defined concept, and that its relation to the physical temperature of a CFT is not universal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entanglement temperature is the temperature of a thermal state that has the same entanglement entropy and the same expectation value of the stress tensor as the ground state.
the entanglement temperature is a universal quantity in any CFT and it characterizes the entanglement structure of excited states in a CFT.
the entanglement temperature is a local quantity in the ground state and the entanglement energy is a local quantity for small perturbations of the ground state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entanglement temperature of the ground state can be interpreted as the local inverse temperature in the dual field theory.

the entanglement temperature can be interpreted as the inverse temperature associated with the reduced density matrix describing the entanglement of the ground state of a CFT with a spherical entangling surface.
entanglement entropy is a local quantity, even when the state is non-uniform, and the entanglement temperature can be used to probe the entanglement properties of a system.
